clue.text: Prat! Can V-1s hit 29/19, perhaps, or his work?

indicators.note: something hit is knocked about and battered, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: V, then the numeral 1 read as the letter I, then S
Mark Francois is a Conservative MP, so he is an example of a Tory

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a Brexiteer MP: could flying bombs strike him, or his book?
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' looks like the V-1s striking, but it is the anagram signal for PRAT + CAN + VIS + TORY. Mark Francois (29/19) is a Brexit-supporting Conservative MP whose self-published book was called Spartan Victory.
explanation.definitionFit: The book Mark Francois wrote and published himself bore this title, so it is literally his work.

clue.text: 1/5 could be what 29/19 didn't want (right in middle of action)

parts.note: Mark Francois campaigned to leave the EU, so the outcome he opposed was Remain

indicators.note: the letter goes into the centre of the word for action, splitting it in two

parts.note: a deed is an action

explanation.surface: A jibe that the Brexiteer's book might end up as unsold stock, the very thing he never wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: Remain was the side Francois opposed in the 2016 referendum. 'in middle of' puts R into DEED to make DERED.
explanation.definitionFit: A remaindered book is unsold stock sold off cheaply by the publisher, a fate the jibe suggests for this one.

indicators.note: the trimmed word presses another piece into its middle, as if squeezing it in
N is short for name, so being nameless means that letter is dropped

parts.note: a person's character is their nature
per is Latin for through, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: An anonymous figure slips through a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' takes away N, the usual short form of name, leaving ATURE; 'squeezes' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is a gap or hole, the sense of an opening as a space something can pass through.

indicators.note: to jar is to jolt or shake, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A kitchen fact: these things are what you open, tins or jars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jars' looks like a noun beside tins, but it is a verb signalling the anagram of TINSOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Intros are introductory passages that begin songs or speeches, so they are what open them.

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for bother is cut off, like an animal losing its tail

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A fox in trouble loses its brush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing tail' drops the final O of TODO.
explanation.definitionFit: Tod is an old Scottish and northern English dialect word for a fox, familiar from crosswords.

clue.text: Heartless Green by clinic perhaps where 1/5's likely to turn up

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters given might be arranged some other way
the heart of a five-letter word is its middle letter, which is removed

parts.note: taken as written, before its middle letter goes

explanation.surface: A Green politician beside a clinic, heartlessly, and a jibe about where the book will land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' takes the central E from GREEN to leave GREN; 'perhaps' then mixes GREN with BY and CLINIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A recycling bin takes unwanted paper, the jibe being that copies of the book will be thrown away.

clue.text: Like 1/5 by British author local was first to describe — awful lot of shit!

parts.note: Will Self is a British novelist
your local is your nearest pub

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: to have led is to have been first

indicators.note: awful marks the letters as being in a terrible state, so they are rearranged
a lot of the word, rather than all of it, means its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A rude review: the book by a British author, celebrated down the pub, is a load of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lot of' trims the last letter, leaving SHI, which 'awful' rearranges; 'to describe' means drawing round, so the leader wraps it. A local is the British name for one's regular pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Francois's book was not taken by a publisher; he paid to bring it out himself.

clue.text: Junk — resort to a bit of mockery

parts.note: a spa is a health resort

indicators.note: only a small bit of the word, its opening letter, is taken

explanation.surface: Rubbish: resorting to mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of' takes M from mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is unsolicited junk email, named after the tinned meat via a Monty Python sketch.

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
during says the answer lies within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A liaison so discreet that the night is never spoken of again.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'during' in the definition, but an affair is the event itself; 'during' signals the letters inside 'night never', and 'recalled' reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair in the sense of an occasion or happening is an event, as in 'a grand affair'.

clue.text: Coppers' old boss and one less senior creak at the edges

parts.note: a DI, detective inspector, ranks below the chief inspector

indicators.note: only the edges of the word, its first and last letters, are used

explanation.surface: A retired police chief and a junior officer, both creaking a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the edges' takes C and K from creak. Cressida Dick was Commissioner of London's Metropolitan Police until 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Cressida Dick formerly headed the Metropolitan Police, so she was the London police force's former head.

clue.text: Painter maybe backing himself — it's about time

indicators.note: going backwards means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the painter himself could be an RA, a Royal Academician

indicators.note: about means turned around and moved about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter turning his back on himself: it's high time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'himself' refers back to the painter, an RA (Royal Academician); 'backing' turns RA into AR, and 'about' rearranges IT'S into TIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter is one kind of artist, hence the 'maybe' marking an example.

indicators.note: the two short pieces go inside the word for a criminal

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who handles stolen goods
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A crook leaves troops stationed in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like an adjective but is the noun: a fence receives stolen goods. 'inside' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is the Tuscan city in Italy, Firenze to Italians.

clue.text: Mortar there exploded causing movement underfoot

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A mortar shell went off and made the ground shake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploded' signals the anagram of MORTARTHERE.
explanation.definitionFit: An earth tremor is a small earthquake, felt as the ground shifting beneath one's feet.

clue.text: Shattering blow — no book refund! Great!

indicators.note: shattering breaks something into pieces, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
B is the abbreviation for book, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written, before its B goes

explanation.surface: A crushing setback: the book can't be returned for your money back. Brilliant!
explanation.walkthrough: 'no book' drops B from BLOW, leaving LOW; 'Shattering' mixes LOW with REFUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of delight, as when someone says 'Wonderful!' or 'Great!' at good news.

clue.text: Working with those people rankled occasionally — self-serving

parts.note: on means working, as in a machine being on
them refers to those people

indicators.note: only now and then is a letter picked, every other one

explanation.surface: Working alongside that lot was a sore point at times; they were only out for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes A, K, E from rankled.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the make is out for their own gain, pursuing advantage selfishly.

clue.text: Intellect of leader of Brexit shower?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a shower is a fall of rain

explanation.surface: A sly dig: is a Brexit leader's intellect just a passing shower?
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader of' takes B from Brexit; 'shower' may also suggest a 'shower' as in a useless bunch, a British slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Brain is used for intelligence or mental capacity, as in 'she has a good brain'.

definitions.meaning: the rear part of a ship

explanation.surface: Returning to the ocean is a tough business.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern names both the rear of a vessel and a severe manner, two unrelated senses.

indicators.note: the letters as given are in doubt, so a different order is wanted

explanation.surface: A huge catch, wasn't it? Not so sure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubtful' signals the anagram of HAULRIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra-high describes something at an extreme level, as in ultra-high frequency.

clue.text: Weird trait — people showing possible employment for 1/5

indicators.note: weird means odd, so the letters are taken in an odd order

explanation.surface: People displaying an odd quality, and a jeer about what the book is good for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weird' signals the anagram of TRAITPEOPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The joke is that the book's pages are only fit for wiping, a use rather than a read.

indicators.note: the letters are set out wrongly and must be put right

parts.note: SS, steamship, is a standard abbreviation for a ship

explanation.surface: A vessel badly loaded is heading for a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incorrectly' rearranges LOADED into DEADLO.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead loss is a complete failure, a person or thing that is useless, a fiasco.

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold or keep, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: 'no way' is an emphatic refusal
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A nation that flatly refuses to keep up the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maintaining' is the container signal; R goes between the two words of the refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is the Scandinavian kingdom, an instance of a country.

parts.note: a means one, as in 'a pound' for one pound
ire is anger or irritation

explanation.surface: Someone expressed annoyance with the department they work in.
explanation.definitionFit: To air a view is to express it, so aired means expressed or spoken out.

parts.note: bar means except or save, as in 'bar none'
B is a short form for Britain or British

explanation.surface: A spur to rescue the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' looks like rescue but means except.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a sharp backward point, and a spur is a sharp projection too, a related sense.

definitions.meaning: a ship that lies to is held stationary facing the wind

explanation.surface: Deceive the crew and bring the vessel to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Lie to is both a phrase for deceiving someone and a nautical term for halting with sails trimmed.

parts.note: a mark is a note, sign or indication
Francisco Franco was dictator of Spain

explanation.surface: A notice that a dictator wrote the book.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Francois is a Conservative MP and Brexit campaigner who self-published the book Spartan Victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Francois wrote and published the book Spartan Victory, so he is its author.

definitions.meaning: The comic strip by Charles Schulz

explanation.surface: Undressing for next to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts is both the name of a famous comic strip and slang for a paltry sum of pay.

clue.text: Extending across river when current is accommodating

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as the sun rose'

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so one piece takes another inside

parts.note: a tide is a current of water

explanation.surface: A bridge spanning a river where the flow makes room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is accommodating' puts R inside TIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Astride means with a leg on each side, so straddling or spanning something.
